name: Release notes
job: Notes written from what merged, and word to everyone who asked for it
intro: Release notes drafts the note from every pull request as it merges, folds out the routine work, and keeps your edits. When the release goes live, publish it to GitHub, a public changelog and Slack, then tell everyone who asked, in the thread they asked in.
does: Every merge redrafts the open note; each line keeps its pull requests and issues, and a line you edited is never rewritten.
Ready when it's live: the deploy workflow's run says so, and the publisher gets a choice in Today.
Each person who asked gets a reply drafted where they asked: their email thread, their GitHub issue or their Slack thread. Nothing is sent until someone presses Send.

accounts.why: One shared GitHub connection for the Lemma: the repositories it watches, and where the release goes.
Optional: the channel the note is posted to.

setup: Once for the whole Lemma: the repositories, how you know a release is live (your deploy workflow, or a tag), an optional Slack channel, and who publishes.
Or look around with a sample release: a made-up product's v2.14, with the people who asked for it.
Each person opens the app once, so replies to the people who asked them can be drafted in their own threads.
